title: Please Hold, I'll Ask My Supervisor

briefing.headline: Contact centres: what you should know before the call
points: Agents answer customer calls about billing, contracts and technical problems.
First-call resolution means the customer's problem is solved in the first call, without a transfer or callback.
Agents often have limits on what they may decide themselves, such as giving a small credit on a bill.
Contact centres track almost everything per agent: call time, transfers, resolution and call reasons.

stakeholder.name: Ines Dumont
stakeholder.org: Telvio, a telecom provider with a 120-agent contact centre in Charleroi
stakeholder.voice: Energetic, warm, very data-literate. Talks in contact-centre jargon but happily explains it. Answers questions fully and with numbers.

frontline.name: Mehdi Benali
frontline.role: Customer service agent, two months in
frontline.voice: Polite, keen, a bit nervous about making mistakes. Speaks French and Dutch.

opening_message: Hello! Our first-call resolution has slipped and my supervisors are drowning in transfers. I think the new agents need more product training. We have a lot of products. Can you help?
surface_ask: More product training for new agents.

gold.real_problem: New agents transfer billing complaints to a supervisor because they don't know they may give a goodwill credit of up to 25 euro themselves. The credit limit used to be on the quick-reference card but disappeared when the policies moved to a new knowledge base in March. Product knowledge is not the gap.
gold.need_statement: New agents need to know and feel confident using their authority to give small goodwill credits on billing complaints. Restoring the limit to the quick-reference card and practising those calls fixes it; more product training does not.

hidden_facts.fact: Most transfers come from agents in their first three months, and most of those are billing complaints, not product questions.
hidden_facts.unlocks_when: The player asks who exactly transfers calls, or what kind of calls get transferred.
hidden_facts.reveal_line: Who? The agents in their first three months, mostly. And when I look at the call reasons... it's billing complaints. Not products at all. Huh.

hidden_facts.fact: Agents may give a goodwill credit of up to 25 euro without asking anyone, but most new agents don't know this and transfer the call to a supervisor instead.
hidden_facts.unlocks_when: The player asks what new agents do now with a billing complaint, or what they are allowed to decide themselves.
hidden_facts.reveal_line: What do they do? They put the customer on hold and call a supervisor. For a 10-euro credit they could give themselves! Up to 25 euro, no questions asked. Apparently nobody told them.

hidden_facts.fact: Transfers started rising in March, when the policies moved to a new knowledge base and the credit limit dropped off the quick-reference card.
hidden_facts.unlocks_when: The player asks since when first-call resolution has slipped, or what changed.
hidden_facts.reveal_line: It started in March. That's when we moved everything into the new knowledge base. The old quick-reference card had the credit limit on it. The new one... doesn't, I think.

hidden_facts.fact: The telephony system tracks first-call resolution and transfers per agent and per call reason.
hidden_facts.unlocks_when: The player asks how first-call resolution is measured or what data is available.
hidden_facts.reveal_line: We measure everything. First-call resolution, transfers, per agent, per call reason. I have dashboards for my dashboards.

constraints.deadline: Before the end-of-year peak in billing calls.
constraints.audience: 120 agents, about 25 of them in their first three months.
constraints.schedule: Agents can be taken off the phones for short sessions in quiet hours.
data_available: First-call resolution and transfers per agent and call reason
Call recordings used for quality checks
data_not_available: Any record of how often agents check the knowledge base

dependencies.concern: Need time to coach new agents on billing calls, and must stop simply taking over the call.
dependencies.if_ignored: Supervisors keep solving the calls themselves and agents never learn.

dependencies.concern: Owns the quick-reference card and the policy pages.
dependencies.if_ignored: The next group of new agents won't find the credit limit either.

traps: Overall first-call resolution for all 120 agents, which hides the new-agent pattern.

gold_plan.baseline: Transfers on billing complaints and first-call resolution for agents in their first three months.
gold_plan.behaviour: New agents give goodwill credits within their limit instead of transferring, checked in a sample of recorded calls.
gold_plan.leading_indicators: Goodwill credits given by new agents; supervisor transfer requests per day.
gold_plan.business_metric: First-call resolution on billing complaints, and supervisor workload.
gold_plan.collection: The telephony dashboard, per agent tenure group and call reason, weekly.

concepts.conventional: More product training for new agents.
concepts.solid: Put the 25-euro credit limit back on the quick-reference card, and run a short practice session for new agents on handling billing complaints with that authority, using real call recordings. Supervisors coach the next few billing calls instead of taking them over.
next_level_examples: Add the goodwill credit to onboarding as a 'you're allowed to' moment, so new agents start with confidence instead of permission-seeking.
Let supervisors answer transfer requests with a question ('what would you do?') rather than taking the call, for the first month.
also_valid: A short refresher on billing products is fine alongside, if the credit authority is the focus.
red_flags: More product training as the main answer.
Training all 120 agents without seeing it's the new ones.
Leaving the quick-reference card as it is.

defence_objections: Let new agents hand out credits on their own? Finance will imagine a river of free money.
Supervisors coaching instead of taking calls? The queue will explode while they ask 'what would you do?'
question_you_didnt_ask: What kind of calls get transferred?
actor_notes: Ines is open and loves data: any question about numbers gets a full answer.
She assumes it's product knowledge until the player asks which calls are transferred; play the 'huh' moment.
She's happy with practical, quick fixes and doesn't need convincing for sensible ideas.
flavour_lines: I have dashboards for my dashboards.
Our hold music is Vivaldi. Customers hear a lot of Vivaldi.

worked_example.note: Mieke's worked example for your very first request: she fills in the concept and the risks so you see a finished case board once.
worked_example.idea: Put the 25-euro credit limit back on the card, let new agents practise billing calls with it, and have supervisors coach instead of taking over.
worked_example.why: New agents don't know they may give a small credit, so they transfer the call. Knowing the limit and practising it fixes that.
worked_example.not: Not more product training: they know the products. These calls are about billing.

risks.mitigation: Ines asks them to coach the next five billing calls, not take them over.
Get the limit back on the card and the policy page before the practice session.
